objectives: Recognise and describe information about health-related topics and issues.
Comprehend and use the Health inquiry model.
Analyse and interpret information to draw conclusions about health-related topics and issues.
Critique information to distinguish determinants that influence health status.
Investigate and synthesise information to develop action strategies.
Evaluate and reflect on implemented action strategies to justify recommendations that mediate, advocate and enable health promotion.
Make decisions about and use mode-appropriate features, language and conventions for particular purposes and contexts.

units.title: Resilience as a personal health resource
units.description: In this introductory unit, students apply a socio-critical lens to explore health as socially constructed, focusing on resilience as a personal health resource. The salutogenic approach, the PERMA+ framework, the personal skills action area of the Ottawa Charter and RE-AIM are used to analyse, implement and evaluate action strategies that build resilience.

units.title: Peers and family as resources for healthy living
units.description: Students plan, implement and evaluate an action strategy to advocate, mediate and enable change in a peer and family health context. One topic is selected from two choices: Elective topic 1: Alcohol, or Elective topic 2: Body image. Approaches include social cognitive theory, the Ottawa Charter and RE-AIM.

units.title: Community as a resource for healthy living
units.description: Students explore the role of the community in shaping health resources through one topic selected from three choices: Elective topic 1: Homelessness, Elective topic 2: Transport safety, or Elective topic 3: Anxiety. Approaches include the social ecological model, the diffusion of innovations model and RE-AIM.

units.title: Respectful relationships in the post-schooling transition
units.description: This culminating unit challenges students to investigate and evaluate innovations that influence respectful relationships to help them navigate the post-schooling life course transition. It uses the life course perspective, the diffusion of innovations model and RE-AIM.

internal_assessment.title: Action research
internal_assessment.description: Internal assessment 1: Action research (25%). Relates to Unit 3; students research one of Elective topic 1: Homelessness, Elective topic 2: Transport safety or Elective topic 3: Anxiety. Must be implemented before IA2.

internal_assessment.title: Extended response
internal_assessment.description: Internal assessment 2: Examination — extended response (25%). Relates to Unit 3 and to the same elective topic as IA1. Students respond to an item with unseen stimulus. Must be implemented after IA1.

internal_assessment.title: Investigation
internal_assessment.description: Internal assessment 3: Investigation (25%). Relates to Unit 4; students investigate the development of respectful relationships as a general resistance resource for a successful post-schooling transition.

external_assessment.title: Extended response
external_assessment.description: External assessment: Examination — extended response (25%). Developed and marked by the QCAA; common to all schools and administered under the same conditions, at the same time, on the same day. Relates to Unit 4.
